claims.text: The driver asked the rider to cancel, and the chat log proves it on its face. MSG-02733-001, sent by the DRIVER at 2026-08-15T07:52:21+08:00 and read by the rider at 07:52:51, says 'sorry got a problem with the car, can you cancel on your side'. The rider replied 'ok cancelling' at 07:53:21 (MSG-02733-002) and the trip was cancelled by the rider at 07:55:21. That is squarely the third exception in POL-NS-10(f) - the driver asked the rider to cancel, and the chat_log shows it. The $4.50 cancellation fee must therefore be refunded to the rider in full, and the rider's own cancellation stops being the operative fact.

The charge is labelled a no-show fee, but no limb of POL-NS-01 holds on this record. The trip record's event chain runs driver_assigned 07:48:21, driver_en_route 07:48:29, trip_cancelled 07:55:21 - there is no driver 'arrived' event anywhere, so limb (a) fails. The driver's own trace then breaks limb (b): across 49 fixes the driver is never once inside the pickup geofence, and the qualifying in-radius fix count is zero. Where the anchor clause fails, the fee is not chargeable under it.

Limb (d) of POL-NS-01 independently fails. The record shows no boarding event and the trip was terminated with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_CANCELLED - not RIDER_NO_SHOW, not RIDER_UNREACHABLE, not EXCESSIVE_WAIT. A no-show fee cannot be built on a cancellation recorded under the rider's ordinary cancellation code; the mis-selected code is a driver-education item, not a basis for keeping the fee.

POL-NS-02 deems a driver arrived only where at least 3 consecutive fixes, each accurate to 25 m or better, fall inside the arrival radius - 50 m for this STANDARD zone class, read from the fee schedule. The driver's trace carries 49 fixes over the window, zero qualifying in-radius fixes, and a minimum distance to the pickup pin of 7000.03 m: the closest he ever came was seven kilometres away. On this trace the driver never arrived, limb (b) of POL-NS-01 fails, and the rider is entitled to a full refund of the cancellation fee.

The softer wrong-entrance route cannot rescue this fee either. POL-NS-03 exists for a driver stationary outside the arrival radius but not more than 400 m from the pin; here the driver's minimum distance was 7.0 km, more than seventeen times that ceiling, so the clause is never engaged and nothing about fault allocation between the parties can displace the refund that POL-NS-02 gives the rider.

The effective in-geofence dwell is zero seconds against the 180 second free waiting period in force for this trip (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec, STANDARD zone) - a shortfall of 180 seconds, with a longest qualifying run of 0 fixes. The driver's recorded speeds across the trace run from 57.2 to 62.9 km/h, which is a driver moving on a road, not a driver holding position at a pickup. Nor can he accumulate dwell: POL-NS-06(i) requires a present, populated traffic_advisory of type KERB_RESTRICTION, ENFORCEMENT, CLOSURE or ACCIDENT, and EV-ADVIS-02733-01 is MISSING (an absent artifact, weight 0.0, which I disclose), so limb (i) is unavailable by its own terms and a MISSING advisory can never reduce the minimum. The full refund stands and no driver compensation is payable.

Every artifact this case turns on is clean, so there is no impairment discount. The fare_breakdown cancellation-fee line is 4.50 and reconciles with platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd of 4.50, so POL-NS-08(d) is not met; the chat carries 2 messages matching trip_record.chat_message_count of 2 with sequence numbering intact, so limb (c) is not met; the trace reports 100.0% coverage at a 10 second cadence with max_gap_sec 0.0, so limb (b) is not met; and the trip record's timestamps align with the trace, so limb (a) is not met. The facts that decide this dispute are carried by artifacts at weight multiplier 1.0 and there is no ground to down-weight them.

No escalation trigger fires, so this dispute should be decided on the merits as a full refund rather than held in human review. rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1, below the 3 that POL-NS-09(d) requires; disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 0 on both profiles, so limb (c) does not fire; and driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 0 against completed_trips_30d of 55, so the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check (4 or more terminations and a rate above 0.08) does not trip. With admissible, complete evidence and no abuse signal on either side, the fee should be returned to the rider now.

The cancellation on this trip was the rider's own act, not a driver termination: trip_record shows cancelled_by 'RIDER' with reason code RIDER_CANCELLED at 2026-08-15T07:55:21, 420 seconds after the 07:48:21 acceptance and well beyond the 180-second grace then in force (trip_record.platform_policy.grace_after_match_sec = 180; the published default in fee_schedule.defaults is the same). Under POL-NS-10(f) a rider's own post-grace cancellation is chargeable at platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd - $4.50 on this record - 'whether or not the driver had arrived', so the starting position on a rider-triggered cancellation is that the $4.50 fee stands, and the driver's arrival is not an element of that charge.

The one exception in POL-NS-10(f) that could rest on the timetable is not engaged. The record assigned the driver at 07:48:21 with an ETA of 15 minutes, i.e. an expected arrival about 08:03, and the rider cancelled at 07:55:21 - roughly eight minutes before the first estimated arrival time shown to her. The GPS trace is consistent with a driver still in transit within that quoted window: 49 fixes between 07:48:21 and 07:56:21, holding between 57.2 and 62.9 km/h throughout, with no stationary interval anywhere in the window. The rider did not cancel because the driver was late against his own ETA; she cancelled before that ETA had even matured.

The amount charged is the platform's own published figure, not an invented one, and the ledger is clean. fare_breakdown.cancellation_fee = $4.50 equals trip_record.platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd = $4.50, which is the net figure the fee_schedule resolution rule produces for this record (the rider's gross figure being $6.61), and EV-FARE-02733 is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, its lines reconciling to total_charged. There is accordingly no fare defect of the kind POL-NS-08(d) contemplates, and no ground to reduce the amount as distinct from the separate question whether it is chargeable at all.

POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider on this record. Limb (a) requires a rider message during the waiting window that is locating or coordinating - her own position, an entrance, block, tower or bay identifier, a request for the driver's position, or a statement that she cannot see the vehicle - and the rider's only message, MSG-02733-002 sent at 07:53:21, reads 'ok cancelling', which identifies no location and asks the driver for nothing. Limb (c) requires the rider's device within the 100 m STANDARD presence radius for the MAJORITY of qualifying fixes across the waiting window, and the rider track carries a single fix, timestamped 07:57:11, which postdates the 07:55:21 cancellation; the record therefore does not place the rider at the pin during the waiting window at all.

POL-NS-06's shortfall route is not the operative test on this trip: it prices the effective in-geofence dwell against the free waiting period on a no-show charge, and this trip carries no driver termination at all - status CANCELLED_BY_RIDER, reason code RIDER_CANCELLED, no 'arrived' event and no boarding event in the trip record. The GPS shows 0 qualifying in-geofence fixes and 0 seconds of dwell, but on a trip the rider cancelled herself the charge (if any) arises under POL-NS-10, and the dwell arithmetic does not by itself carry it. The driver likewise does not invoke POL-NS-06(i): no traffic advisory covers Blk 231 Serangoon Ave 3 in this window - EV-ADVIS-02733-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT - so limb (i)'s aggregation is unavailable and the driver claims nothing under it.

Nothing in the party profiles supports an adverse finding against the driver, and no escalation trigger is engaged on his side. The POL-NS-07 anti-farming check reads driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d = 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_30d = 55, so neither limb of that test (4 or more terminations, and a rate above 0.08) is met; and rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d = 1 is below the 3 that POL-NS-09(d) requires. Both profile artifacts are COMPLETE at weight 1.0, and no other profile field is relied on.

The driver does not contest the operation of the POL-NS-10(f) exception on this record, and will not stretch the point: MSG-02733-001, sent by the driver at 07:52:21 and read by the rider within the half-minute, states a problem with the car and asks her to 'cancel on your side', and POL-NS-10(f) refunds the fee in full where the chat_log shows the driver asked the rider to cancel. The driver's case is therefore confined to what the record does support: that this was a rider-triggered, post-grace cancellation rather than a driver-terminated no-show; that the amount charged is the platform's own published $4.50 and the ledger is unblemished; and that any refund runs to the cancellation-fee line of $4.50 only - no waiting-time fee was charged (waiting_time_fee = $0.00, and POL-NS-10(d) bars charging both on one trip) and nothing beyond the contested $4.50 is returnable.

ruling.explanation:
The $4.50 cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-02733 is refunded to the rider in full.

For the driver: your case starts from a correct proposition. The rider cancelled the trip herself at 07:55:21, 420 seconds after the 07:48:21 acceptance, so the 180-second grace in trip_record.platform_policy.grace_after_match_sec had expired, and under POL-NS-10(f) a rider's own post-grace cancellation is chargeable at platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd ($4.50 on this record) whether or not you had arrived. But the same limb of the same clause refunds the fee in full where the chat_log shows the driver asked the rider to cancel, and that is exactly what this record shows: MSG-02733-001, sent by you at 07:52:21 and read at 07:52:51, reads 'sorry got a problem with the car, can you cancel on your side', and the rider replied 'ok cancelling' at 07:53:21 (MSG-02733-002). Your own advocate concedes the point. Your ETA argument does not rescue the fee: the exception turns on your request, not on whether you were running late, and in any event the rider cancelled roughly eight minutes before the 08:03 arrival time quoted to her. Your point that the fare ledger is clean is accepted (fare_breakdown.cancellation_fee $4.50 equals platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd $4.50, and EV-FARE-02733 is COMPLETE at weight 1.0), but a correctly computed amount is not a chargeable one.

Independently, the no-show foundation fails and would give the rider the same refund. POL-NS-01 requires a driver 'arrived' event (the trip record has none - its event chain is driver_assigned, driver_en_route, trip_cancelled), fixes inside the pickup geofence (the driver's closest approach to the pin is 7,000.03 m, and across 49 fixes he holds 57.2-62.9 km/h with 0 qualifying in-geofence fixes), and a termination under RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT (the record shows RIDER_CANCELLED). POL-NS-02 accordingly also entitles the rider to the full fee back, and POL-NS-03 is not engaged because 7.0 km is far beyond its 400 m ceiling.

For the rider: your claims are accepted. The driver's request to cancel is decisive under POL-NS-10(f); the driver never arrived (limbs (a), (b) and (d) of POL-NS-01 all fail); POL-NS-04 need not exonerate you because you win on POL-NS-10(f) regardless; and every artifact this ruling rests on is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so there is no impairment discount. The one absent artifact, EV-ADVIS-02733-01 (TRAFFIC_ADVISORY, MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT), carries no fact here and is not relied on: no advisory covers Blk 231 Serangoon Ave 3, so POL-NS-06(i) dwell aggregation is unavailable, but the refund does not depend on it.

Amount and compensation: $4.50 is refunded, being the contested cancellation-fee line of EV-FARE-02733 and matching platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd; no waiting-time fee was charged (waiting_time_fee $0.00) and none is due, since POL-NS-10(d) bars charging both on one trip. No driver compensation is payable: POL-NS-07 pays the driver only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and it is not, so the anti-farming check never comes into play.

No escalation: POL-NS-09 is not triggered - rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1 (below 3), disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 0 on both profiles, and the POL-NS-07 anti-farming test does not trip - and confidence is above the 0.70 floor. The monetary effect ($4.50) is below the $8.00 execution threshold, so this refund executes automatically.

ruling.explanation:
Addressed to both parties. The $4.50 cancellation fee on trip TRP-02733 is refunded in full to the rider, and no driver compensation is payable to the driver. Both briefs agree on this outcome and the record supports it.

The governing clause is POL-NS-10. The rider cancelled her own booking at 2026-08-15T07:55:21, 420 seconds after the trip was accepted at 07:48:21, so she cancelled outside the 180-second grace then in force (trip_record.platform_policy.grace_after_match_sec = 180, the same figure as fee_schedule.defaults), and under POL-NS-10(f) the fee would ordinarily stand at the platform's published $4.50 'whether or not the driver had arrived'. The driver's submissions on the timetable (POL-NS-10, second claim: ETA about 08:03, rider cancelled about eight minutes before it matured) are correct but do not matter, because a different limb (f) exception applies. That limb refunds the fee in full where the chat_log shows the driver asked the rider to cancel, and EV-CHAT-02733 (COMPLETE, weight_multiplier 1.0) shows exactly that: MSG-02733-001, sent by the DRIVER at 07:52:21 and read by the rider at 07:52:51, reads 'sorry got a problem with the car, can you cancel on your side', and the rider replied 'ok cancelling' at 07:53:21. That is the driver's own contemporaneous statement made from inside the disputed window and an admission against his own interest; it would establish why the trip ended even if the instrument evidence were removed, so it independently carries the deciding fact. The driver's brief concedes the same point. The refund is the cancellation-fee line of $4.50 only (EV-FARE-02733 total_charged = 4.50, cancellation_fee = 4.50); no waiting-time fee was charged (waiting_time_fee = $0.00, and POL-NS-10(d) bars charging both on one trip), and nothing beyond the contested $4.50 is returnable.

The no-show route fails on its own terms and points the same way. POL-NS-01 limb (a) is not met, because EV-TRIP-02733 contains no driver 'arrived' event (its chain runs driver_assigned 07:48:21, driver_en_route 07:48:29, trip_cancelled 07:55:21), and limb (d) is not met, because the trip was terminated with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_CANCELLED rather than RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT. POL-NS-02 is not satisfied either: EV-GPS-02733 carries 49 fixes between 07:48:21 and 07:56:21, none within the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, with a minimum distance to the pickup pin of 7,000.03 m and speeds of 57.2 to 62.9 km/h throughout, so the driver never came near Blk 231 Serangoon Ave 3. POL-NS-03 does not engage: its 400 m wrong-entrance ceiling is exceeded many times over. POL-NS-04 does not exonerate the rider and is not needed here: her only message ('ok cancelling') identifies no location and asks the driver nothing, and her single rider fix (07:57:11) postdates the cancellation.

No driver compensation. POL-NS-07 requires POL-NS-01 to hold in full, which it does not, and the POL-NS-03(ii) pin-ambiguity goodwill is unavailable because the driver was never stationary near the pin. The POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip (driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d = 0 against completed_trips_30d = 55, so neither the 4-or-more limb nor the above-0.08 rate limb is met), and no POL-NS-09 trigger fires: rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d = 1 is below the 3 that limb (d) requires, disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 0 on both profiles so limb (c) does not fire, and no direct contradiction or impairment engages limbs (b) or (e).

Evidence integrity and the discarded claim. The doubt raised by the discarded rider claim does not move the outcome. That claim cited the absent traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02733-01 (weight 0.0) without naming its issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and was discarded under POL-GEN-02(1); in any event nothing here is decided under POL-NS-06(i), because this trip carries no driver termination and no arrival marker. The artifacts that do carry the deciding fact — EV-CHAT-02733, EV-TRIP-02733 and EV-FARE-02733 — are all COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap on this ruling is 1.0 and confidence is 0.95, above the 0.70 escalation floor.

Referrals and execution. No referral is produced: no arrival marker was ever set, so POL-NS-05(ii) has no false-arrival to record; the reason code RIDER_CANCELLED was correctly recorded for the rider's own cancellation rather than mis-selected, so POL-NS-01's driver-education item is not engaged; and no other clause adds an instruction. The monetary effect of $4.50 is below the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold of $8.00 and, no safety or complaint flag being set, this ruling executes automatically, subject to the appeal route under POL-GEN-04.

ruling.explanation: Rider and driver: the $4.50 cancellation fee charged on TRP-02733 is refunded in full to the rider. The charge stands or falls under POL-NS-10, the only clause that decides a fee a rider's own cancellation triggers, and its limb (f) refunds the fee in full where the chat log shows the driver asked the rider to cancel. It does: MSG-02733-001, sent by the DRIVER at 07:52:21, reads 'sorry got a problem with the car, can you cancel on your side', and the rider's MSG-02733-002 at 07:53:21 answers 'ok cancelling'. She cancelled at 07:55:21 — 420 seconds after acceptance, past the 180-second grace_after_match_sec in force — so the fee would prima facie be chargeable under POL-NS-10(f), but the driver-requested-cancellation exception applies and the fee is refunded in full. The DRIVER advocate's own framing is accepted: this was a rider-triggered, post-grace cancellation rather than a driver-terminated no-show, and the refund runs to the cancellation-fee line of $4.50 only. No waiting-time fee was charged (waiting_time_fee $0.00) and POL-NS-10(d) bars both on one trip, so nothing beyond $4.50 is returnable. The no-show anchor fails independently as well: POL-NS-01 needs a driver 'arrived' event (none exists), in-geofence presence (the driver's trace carries 0 qualifying in-radius fixes, closest approach 7,000.03 m from the pin) and a termination under RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT — the record reads RIDER_CANCELLED. POL-NS-02 confirms the driver never arrived, and POL-NS-03 never engages (its 400 m ceiling is exceeded many times over). I do not accept the rider's rider-education suggestion of a mis-selected reason code: the rider cancelled her own trip and RIDER_CANCELLED is the correct code for that, so no clause produces a referral on these facts. On the remaining points: the fare ledger is clean — $4.50 equals platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd and reconciles to total_charged, so POL-NS-08(d) is not met and there is no basis to reduce the amount; POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider (her only message 'ok cancelling' identifies no location, and her single rider-track fix at 07:57:11 postdates the cancellation), but that does not matter because the refund comes from POL-NS-10(f), not POL-NS-04; POL-NS-06's dwell arithmetic is not the operative test on a rider-cancelled trip and the driver claims nothing under its limb (i). No escalation trigger fires: confidence is above the 0.70 floor; both tracks and the ledger are COMPLETE at weight 1.0 with no contradiction; disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 0 on both profiles; rider no_show_disputes_30d is 1 (below 3); and the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip (no_show_terminations_30d 0, rate 0.0). Every artifact carrying the deciding facts — the chat log, the trip record and the GPS trace — is at weight 1.0; the only impaired artifact is the MISSING traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02733-01 at weight 0.0, which carries no fact this ruling rests on. The $4.50 refund is below the $8.00 execution threshold and executes automatically.

ruling.explanation:
Rider and driver: the $4.50 cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-02733 (EV-FARE-02733, cancellation_fee $4.50, total_charged $4.50, payment_status CHARGED) is refunded to the rider in full.

What the record shows. The driver accepted the job at 07:48:21 and set off; at 07:52:21 he messaged the rider, "sorry got a problem with the car, can you cancel on your side" (MSG-02733-001, EV-CHAT-02733, read by the rider at 07:52:51). The rider replied "ok cancelling" at 07:53:21 and cancelled the trip at 07:55:21 (EV-TRIP-02733, cancelled_by RIDER, reason code RIDER_CANCELLED).

The driver's position, accepted. The driver is right that this was a rider-triggered cancellation made 420 seconds after acceptance, beyond the 180-second grace in trip_record.platform_policy.grace_after_match_sec, and that under POL-NS-10(f) such a cancellation is chargeable at platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd, $4.50, "whether or not the driver had arrived". He is also right that the fare ledger is clean: $4.50 equals platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd, so no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect exists, and his point that the ETA exception is not engaged (the driver was still moving at 57.2-62.9 km/h when the rider cancelled) is accepted.

But POL-NS-10(f) carries a further exception, and it decides the case: the fee "is refunded in full where the record shows ... the driver asked the rider to cancel (chat_log)". The chat log shows exactly that, in the driver's own words and timestamp. The driver's advocate concedes this on the record. The refund therefore follows, and it is a full refund of the cancellation-fee line.

The rider's no-show route, accepted as far as it goes but not the operative ground. The rider is right that the charge cannot be sustained as a no-show fee: there is no 'arrived' event and no boarding event in the trip record, the termination is recorded as CANCELLED_BY_RIDER / RIDER_CANCELLED rather than a no-show code, so POL-NS-01 limbs (a) and (d) fail; and the driver's own trace carries 0 qualifying in-geofence fixes with a minimum distance of 7,000.03 m (7.0 km) across 49 fixes, so POL-NS-02 finds no arrival and POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails. POL-NS-03 does not change this: it engages only within 400 m of the pin, and the closest the driver came was 7.0 km, so no wrong-entrance outcome - and no POL-NS-03(ii) pin-ambiguity goodwill - is available. These clauses point the same way as POL-NS-10(f); the fee is refunded because the driver asked for the cancellation, and would also fail as a no-show charge in any event.

Claims that do not move the outcome. POL-NS-04 is not needed: the rider's "ok cancelling" message is not a locating or coordinating message and her single rider fix is timed 07:57:11, after the 07:55:21 cancellation, so that clause would not exonerate her on its own tests - but the refund does not depend on it. The POL-NS-06 dwell arithmetic likewise decides nothing here: the disputed $4.50 is a cancellation fee on a rider-cancelled trip, decided under POL-NS-10.

Driver compensation. None is payable. POL-NS-10(f) is a full refund of the fee and carries no driver payment, and the POL-NS-07 anti-farming test is not reached because POL-NS-01 is not satisfied; the POL-NS-03(ii) goodwill route is unavailable for the distance reason above.

Escalation and referrals. No POL-NS-09 trigger fires: disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 0 on both profiles (limb (c)), rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1 against the 3 limb (d) requires, the anti-farming check reads driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d = 0 against completed_trips_30d = 55 (limb (d)), no two admissible artifacts contradict each other (limb (b)), and the deciding fact is not carried solely by an impaired artifact (limb (e)). No clause produces a referral: no arrival marker was tapped, so POL-NS-05(ii)'s false-arrival record does not fire, and POL-NS-01's driver-education referral is confined to a mis-selected reason code on an in-radius arrival, which is not this case. The reason code RIDER_CANCELLED correctly describes a rider cancellation.

Impairment and confidence. EV-ADVIS-02733-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT); this ruling does not rely on it. The rider's POL-NS-06 dwell claim, which cited that missing artifact without naming its issue code, was discarded at the mechanical check and supports nothing. The deciding fact - that the driver asked the rider to cancel - is carried by the chat log EV-CHAT-02733 at weight 1.0, and the amount by the fare breakdown EV-FARE-02733 at weight 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0 and confidence is 0.95, above the 0.70 policy floor. The monetary effect of $4.50 does not exceed the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold of $8.00, so it executes automatically. This is a provisional ruling and either party may appeal under POL-GEN-04.

ledger.claim: The driver asked the rider to cancel, and the chat log proves it on its face. MSG-02733-001, sent by the DRIVER at 2026-08-15T07:52:21+08:00 and read by the rider at 07:52:51, says 'sorry got a problem with the car, can you cancel on your side'. The rider replied 'ok cancelling' at 07:53:21 (MSG-02733-002) and the trip was cancelled by the rider at 07:55:21. That is squarely the third exception in POL-NS-10(f) - the driver asked the rider to cancel, and the chat_log shows it. The $4.50 cancellation fee must therefore be refunded to the rider in full, and the rider's own cancellation stops being the operative fact.

The charge is labelled a no-show fee, but no limb of POL-NS-01 holds on this record. The trip record's event chain runs driver_assigned 07:48:21, driver_en_route 07:48:29, trip_cancelled 07:55:21 - there is no driver 'arrived' event anywhere, so limb (a) fails. The driver's own trace then breaks limb (b): across 49 fixes the driver is never once inside the pickup geofence, and the qualifying in-radius fix count is zero. Where the anchor clause fails, the fee is not chargeable under it.

Limb (d) of POL-NS-01 independently fails. The record shows no boarding event and the trip was terminated with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_CANCELLED - not RIDER_NO_SHOW, not RIDER_UNREACHABLE, not EXCESSIVE_WAIT. A no-show fee cannot be built on a cancellation recorded under the rider's ordinary cancellation code; the mis-selected code is a driver-education item, not a basis for keeping the fee.

POL-NS-02 deems a driver arrived only where at least 3 consecutive fixes, each accurate to 25 m or better, fall inside the arrival radius - 50 m for this STANDARD zone class, read from the fee schedule. The driver's trace carries 49 fixes over the window, zero qualifying in-radius fixes, and a minimum distance to the pickup pin of 7000.03 m: the closest he ever came was seven kilometres away. On this trace the driver never arrived, limb (b) of POL-NS-01 fails, and the rider is entitled to a full refund of the cancellation fee.

The softer wrong-entrance route cannot rescue this fee either. POL-NS-03 exists for a driver stationary outside the arrival radius but not more than 400 m from the pin; here the driver's minimum distance was 7.0 km, more than seventeen times that ceiling, so the clause is never engaged and nothing about fault allocation between the parties can displace the refund that POL-NS-02 gives the rider.

ledger.claim: Every artifact this case turns on is clean, so there is no impairment discount. The fare_breakdown cancellation-fee line is 4.50 and reconciles with platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd of 4.50, so POL-NS-08(d) is not met; the chat carries 2 messages matching trip_record.chat_message_count of 2 with sequence numbering intact, so limb (c) is not met; the trace reports 100.0% coverage at a 10 second cadence with max_gap_sec 0.0, so limb (b) is not met; and the trip record's timestamps align with the trace, so limb (a) is not met. The facts that decide this dispute are carried by artifacts at weight multiplier 1.0 and there is no ground to down-weight them.

No escalation trigger fires, so this dispute should be decided on the merits as a full refund rather than held in human review. rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1, below the 3 that POL-NS-09(d) requires; disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 0 on both profiles, so limb (c) does not fire; and driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 0 against completed_trips_30d of 55, so the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check (4 or more terminations and a rate above 0.08) does not trip. With admissible, complete evidence and no abuse signal on either side, the fee should be returned to the rider now.

The cancellation on this trip was the rider's own act, not a driver termination: trip_record shows cancelled_by 'RIDER' with reason code RIDER_CANCELLED at 2026-08-15T07:55:21, 420 seconds after the 07:48:21 acceptance and well beyond the 180-second grace then in force (trip_record.platform_policy.grace_after_match_sec = 180; the published default in fee_schedule.defaults is the same). Under POL-NS-10(f) a rider's own post-grace cancellation is chargeable at platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd - $4.50 on this record - 'whether or not the driver had arrived', so the starting position on a rider-triggered cancellation is that the $4.50 fee stands, and the driver's arrival is not an element of that charge.

The one exception in POL-NS-10(f) that could rest on the timetable is not engaged. The record assigned the driver at 07:48:21 with an ETA of 15 minutes, i.e. an expected arrival about 08:03, and the rider cancelled at 07:55:21 - roughly eight minutes before the first estimated arrival time shown to her. The GPS trace is consistent with a driver still in transit within that quoted window: 49 fixes between 07:48:21 and 07:56:21, holding between 57.2 and 62.9 km/h throughout, with no stationary interval anywhere in the window. The rider did not cancel because the driver was late against his own ETA; she cancelled before that ETA had even matured.

The amount charged is the platform's own published figure, not an invented one, and the ledger is clean. fare_breakdown.cancellation_fee = $4.50 equals trip_record.platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd = $4.50, which is the net figure the fee_schedule resolution rule produces for this record (the rider's gross figure being $6.61), and EV-FARE-02733 is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, its lines reconciling to total_charged. There is accordingly no fare defect of the kind POL-NS-08(d) contemplates, and no ground to reduce the amount as distinct from the separate question whether it is chargeable at all.

POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider on this record. Limb (a) requires a rider message during the waiting window that is locating or coordinating - her own position, an entrance, block, tower or bay identifier, a request for the driver's position, or a statement that she cannot see the vehicle - and the rider's only message, MSG-02733-002 sent at 07:53:21, reads 'ok cancelling', which identifies no location and asks the driver for nothing. Limb (c) requires the rider's device within the 100 m STANDARD presence radius for the MAJORITY of qualifying fixes across the waiting window, and the rider track carries a single fix, timestamped 07:57:11, which postdates the 07:55:21 cancellation; the record therefore does not place the rider at the pin during the waiting window at all.

POL-NS-06's shortfall route is not the operative test on this trip: it prices the effective in-geofence dwell against the free waiting period on a no-show charge, and this trip carries no driver termination at all - status CANCELLED_BY_RIDER, reason code RIDER_CANCELLED, no 'arrived' event and no boarding event in the trip record. The GPS shows 0 qualifying in-geofence fixes and 0 seconds of dwell, but on a trip the rider cancelled herself the charge (if any) arises under POL-NS-10, and the dwell arithmetic does not by itself carry it. The driver likewise does not invoke POL-NS-06(i): no traffic advisory covers Blk 231 Serangoon Ave 3 in this window - EV-ADVIS-02733-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT - so limb (i)'s aggregation is unavailable and the driver claims nothing under it.

Nothing in the party profiles supports an adverse finding against the driver, and no escalation trigger is engaged on his side. The POL-NS-07 anti-farming check reads driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d = 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_30d = 55, so neither limb of that test (4 or more terminations, and a rate above 0.08) is met; and rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d = 1 is below the 3 that POL-NS-09(d) requires. Both profile artifacts are COMPLETE at weight 1.0, and no other profile field is relied on.

The driver does not contest the operation of the POL-NS-10(f) exception on this record, and will not stretch the point: MSG-02733-001, sent by the driver at 07:52:21 and read by the rider within the half-minute, states a problem with the car and asks her to 'cancel on your side', and POL-NS-10(f) refunds the fee in full where the chat_log shows the driver asked the rider to cancel. The driver's case is therefore confined to what the record does support: that this was a rider-triggered, post-grace cancellation rather than a driver-terminated no-show; that the amount charged is the platform's own published $4.50 and the ledger is unblemished; and that any refund runs to the cancellation-fee line of $4.50 only - no waiting-time fee was charged (waiting_time_fee = $0.00, and POL-NS-10(d) bars charging both on one trip) and nothing beyond the contested $4.50 is returnable.
